### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /meta/object/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/core.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `26c3687812e599f309b852dab94771c4258d7f7f` — the merge of head `c60b83fa41c5fa1987beabb82baf38575638d64c` into base `f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 26c3687812e599f309b852dab94771c4258d7f7f && git checkout 26c3687812e599f309b852dab94771c4258d7f7f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8 c60b83fa41c5fa1987beabb82baf38575638d64c && git checkout -B drift-repro f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8 && git merge --no-ff c60b83fa41c5fa1987beabb82baf38575638d64c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f6902e950023df8ff5285632d9b798e4a2e0a8d8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：保存被拒、没有权限时的提示里出现的字段名、选项名、对象名，现在跟表单上显示的一致。比如应用用英文编写、默认给用户中文，英文用户看到的提示也是英文名称，不会再夹杂中文。
- 为什么做：以前表单是一种语言，报错里的名字却是另一种，用户对不上号。
- 出错会怎样：只影响提示里的名称文字，拒不拒绝的判断没变；繁体中文请求会和页面一样读简体中文的名称。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事。它给一个对外公开的函数参数多加了一个可选项，席位会安排一次约定审核，然后由区域落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `b5b0fd289d088e4a881958c299dabe2976732113` · 2026-11-19T07:36Z

- **形态** — 19 files, +864/−121 (985 lines), across `objectql`, `plugin-security`, and two test files in `rest` / `service-automation`; plus one changeset. No `packages/spec/src` path. Base `8b550f81`, K=1 after the area's clean main merge. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35351`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit.
- **Fixes vs card #34030 (route A)**:
  - `resolveFieldLabel`, `resolveOptionLabel` and `objectDisplayLabel` drop their `t()` key probes and ask `translatedLabels(doc, ctx)`. It runs `translateObject` from `@objectstack/spec/system`, the `/meta` translator, over a document holding only the declared labels. A throw returns the declared document, so a misbehaving i18n service still cannot turn a 400/409 into a 500.
  - `validationMessageContext` adds a lazy, memoised `labelTranslation` thunk. Its `labelTranslationOf` builds the bundle from `getLocales()`/`getTranslations()` and builds `ResolveOptions` as `{ locale, fallbackChain: [getFallbackLocale()], defaultLocale: getSourceLocale() ?? getDefaultLocale() }`, the same shape the metadata route uses. Each getter is feature-detected.
  - `plugin-security`'s `denialLabels` does the same for `masterGateDenialMessage` and `fieldEditDenialMessage`.
  - The option lookup keeps the field-then-picklist chain, because `translateObject` walks it given `picklist`.
  - `t()` keeps messages only.
- **Point 1 — `Clause-②`: declaration change required → `yes (widening)`.** `ValidationMessageContext` gains the optional `labelTranslation`, plus the new `ValidationLabelTranslation` shape. Both are reachable in the published `.d.ts` through `validateRecord`'s `options.messages`, and `validateRecord` is exported from `@objectstack/objectql`'s `.` entry (`index.ts:606`). The fleet declares a widened published export as `yes (widening)`. This is the same ruling as #35374 (`mergeSeedDatasets` gaining `owner`) and the precedent of the 35147 and 34779 changesets. Change the line in the changeset and in the PR body; `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` stay. **For the L2 to rule on the arm:** a direct `validateRecord` caller that passes only `messages.translate` used to get translated labels and now gets declared ones. The changeset discloses this for t()-only doubles. In-repo there is no such caller outside `objectql`: `plugin-security`'s `cbp-write-gate` mentions `validateRecord` only in comments, and `ui/core` has its own function of that name. I read it as a moved answer on an optional channel, not a refusal. The L2 confirms `widening` or moves it to `narrowing`.
- **Point 2 — `fieldEditDenialMessage` under the bounded in-place exemption: accepted.** It is the same defect class in the same claimed file, and a red pin is cited. The rewrite also hoists the unreadable-field check ahead of the label pass. That gives the same opaque answer as before, because both orders return `field_edit_denied_opaque`.
- **Point 3 — re-spelled `t()`-only doubles: accepted.** They hand the same rows over through `getLocales`/`getTranslations`, and no assertion is weakened. Two of them are outside the claim (`rest` `data-not-null-field-label-24715`, `service-automation` `flow-write-refusal-locale`). They are test-only, and needed because a t()-only double no longer translates labels; that CI red was the doubles, not a missed code path. **Nit:** list both in the PR body's Tests section (the final-head comment records them).
- **Point 4 — changeset behaviour notes: accepted.** Each of the four follows from asking `translateObject` with `/meta`'s options, and each is stated: t()-only doubles, the in-memory fallback with no `getFallbackLocale`, the built-in labels of injected system fields, and `zh-TW` → `zh-CN` rows. Read sentence by sentence against the diff: they match.
- **Pins:**
  - `engine-label-source-locale.test.ts`: field, option (`invalid_transition`) and object (`DELETE_RESTRICTED`) in `sourceLocale: 'en'` / `defaultLocale: 'zh-CN'` read the English labels. CONTROLs: a zh-CN request still reads zh-CN, and with no `sourceLocale` an en request walks to zh-CN as before.
  - `denial-label-source-locale.test.ts`: the same matrix for the master gate and the field-edit gate.
  - The existing duplicate, delete-restricted, restore, not-null, state-machine and owner-queue pins are carried to the new channel.
- **门禁** — 53 check-runs on this head: 37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure.
- **范围外去向:**
  - (a) `plugin-approvals` `readerLabelsFor` / the approval notification subject and the `plugin-audit` activity summary still read labels through `t()`. Same class, pre-existing, not blocking. Route: ux-3 files its drafted card, nested under #34030.
  - (b) `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:50-53` and eval case 11 go stale on landing. That is a governed path; ux-3 has already routed it to seat 5.
- **L2 owed (routing)** — after the declaration change, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` → seat 5 routes the contract review, including the arm question in Point 1.
- **落地条款** — not governed. Push only the declaration change and the PR-body nit. This ACCEPT carries over to that head if it contains nothing else, a main merge included. ux-3 lands after the seat's L2 record.

repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbUb7TcZK1XUAddUmQ

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `caf89b8bc928f6b8dff14b6276a56f65f29393df`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #34030 (body and all 7 comments, including the claim, the os-dev report 7001158402 and carrier note 6999412689); PR #35351 (body, 19-file list, net diff against `main` at this head); the 57 check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ValidationMessageContext.labelTranslation?` (new optional member): a widening, and correctly named one.** The interface is not exported by name. It is still published, because it is the type of `ValidateRecordOptions.messages` (`validateRecord`, `.` entry, `index.ts:606`) and of `EvaluateRulesOptions.messages`. `EvaluateRulesOptions` is a named type export on both `.` and `./core`, and `evaluateValidationRules` is exported from both. An object literal that was valid before is still valid.
- **`translatedLabels` and `ValidationLabelTranslation` are exported from the module only.** Neither is re-exported from `index.ts` or `core.ts`, so neither is a public surface. Right.
- **`ValidationMessageContext.translate` no longer translates labels. This is a narrowing, and it was declared wrong.** On `main`, the published jsdoc of `translate` said it is "used for two things: a deployment's `validation.field.*` message override, and the field's TRANSLATED label". At this head, `resolveFieldLabel`, `resolveOptionLabel` and `objectDisplayLabel` read only `labelTranslation`. Take a direct caller of `validateRecord` or `evaluateValidationRules` that passes `messages: { locale, objectName, translate }`, the shape the jsdoc described. Without changing its code, it now gets the declared labels in every locale, not the translated ones. That covers field labels, `invalid_transition` option labels and `requiredWhen` field labels. The PR's own pin is the evidence. `record-validator.test.ts` "prefers the translated label over the declared one" had to change its INPUT, adding `labelTranslation`, to keep its expected output. With the old call shape it now answers `Penalty Amount`. See the ruling in ②.
- **Engine write path (`validationMessageContext` → `labelTranslationOf`): right.** `getLocales` and `getTranslations` are REQUIRED members of `II18nService` (`contracts/i18n-service.ts:33,46`), so every conforming service still translates engine refusals. The only change is that the answer now follows the `/meta` rule (`translateObject`, with `fallbackChain` set to the declared fallback and `defaultLocale` set to `sourceLocale`, else `defaultLocale`). The thunk is lazy and memoised per context. A throw returns the declared document, so a 400 or 409 still cannot become a 500. The card's ask under route (A) is met, and `t()` and `contracts/i18n-service.ts` are untouched.
- **Disclosed moved answers on the engine path are accepted.** The changeset states each of them, and each matches what `/meta` serves for the same request:
  - `createMemoryI18n` has no `getFallbackLocale`. A request in a locale with no bundle now gets the declared label instead of the default-locale row.
  - Injected system fields get the built-in translation.
  - zh-TW reads the zh-CN rows in the security layer.
- **Accept sets: no change.** No write is newly refused or newly admitted, and every verdict, code and status is unchanged. Only the human text of refusals moves.
- **Private engine method `objectDisplayLabel`: no public surface.** Its ctx type became `Pick` of `locale` and `labelTranslation`. `duplicate-record-error.ts` spreads the full context into `resolveFieldLabel` and `objectDisplayLabel` (`{ ...messages, objectName }`), so the thunk reaches it. Its `Pick` of `locale` and `translate` covers sentence rendering only. Right.
- **plugin-security `denialLabels` matches the objectql change.** It builds the bundle from `getLocales()` and `getTranslations()` with the same feature detection. It builds the same `ResolveOptions` (`locale`, the declared `fallbackChain`, then `sourceLocale` else `defaultLocale`). It calls the same translator, `translateObject`, and keeps the declared document on a throw. Labels are resolved in the language the sentence resolves to (`denialLocaleOf`), and objectql resolves them in the negotiated request locale that its sentence renders in. So in both packages the labels follow their own sentence.
  - The `fieldEditDenialMessage` rewrite moves the unreadable-field check ahead of the label pass. Both orders return `field_edit_denied_opaque`, so the change is equivalent.
  - `masterGateDenialMessage` keeps its `label === master` guard against the API name.
  - Everything in plugin-security is file-private, so it has no public surface.

### ② Semver level

- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No key, accepted value, metadata type, requirement or default that an author can write changes. The runtime now does what `TranslationConfigSchema.sourceLocale`'s existing `.describe` already promised ("a request in this locale is answered from the inline text"), so the meaning of the key does not change. It is not `semantic`.
- **`patch` for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/plugin-security`: right.** The level follows the protocol kind alone. `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change still ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist item 3). plugin-security moves no public surface. Both `Check Changeset` runs on this head succeeded.
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`: WRONG ARM. MUST-FIX M1.**
  - **Ruling: a narrowing.** The optional member is a widening, and that fact stands. Separately, the diff takes a declared capability away from an existing consumer of a published input channel: the label translation that `translate` was documented to perform.
  - **Why it is not "a moved answer on an optional channel".** `translate` is optional, but the caller has already opted in to it. An opted-in caller now gets degraded output with no code change of its own, and it gets its old output back only by adopting a NEW member. A widening leaves every existing caller's observable output as it was. This change does not.
  - **What does not decide it.** Nothing is refused, and no out-of-package caller exists in the repo. The arm is judged against the published `.d.ts` and its documented behaviour, not against the in-repo caller count. The change is also not a fix for such a caller: with no `sourceLocale` and an ordinary bundle, its old labels were correct, and they are now lost in every locale.
  - **The required arm is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`** (clause2-line: "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read"). It goes on the line-initial declaration in BOTH the PR body and `.changeset/34030-refusal-labels-source-locale.md`.
  - **What the changeset must then carry.**
    - The BREAKING banner.
    - The migration, as FROM, then TO, then the one-line fix. FROM: `messages: { locale, objectName, translate }` translated field, option and object labels through `translate`. TO: labels are read only through `messages.labelTranslation`. Fix: pass `labelTranslation: () => ({ bundle, options })`, where `bundle` is a `TranslationBundle` keyed by locale and `options` is a `ResolveOptions` from `@objectstack/spec/system`.
    - Exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker. `check:adr-0087-registration` prints the closed set. `runtime-interface-only` reads as the fitting category for a runtime API with no metadata change, but the gate decides.
    - `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` stay.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** none (`[]` in os-dev report 7001158402). Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flag `dogfood_battery: n/a — no (narrowing) arm`: overturned by M1.** With the `(narrowing)` arm, a full `dogfood_battery` pinned to the re-declared head is owed before the queue, with every red fixed or reported (the L1 review checklist rule for `(narrowing)`). On this head the PR-side `Dogfood Regression Gate (shard/3)` run was `skipped`, and only the umbrella `Dogfood Regression Gate` reported `success`, so no battery has run against this diff yet.
- **Dev reading A1 ("no Clause-② yes"):** superseded, first by the L1 ACCEPT (7002854859, Point 1, which referred the arm to this review) and now by M1.
- **Out of scope (a): readers still on `t()` (plugin-approvals `readerLabelsFor` and `subjectParams`, plugin-audit `activity-summary-message.ts`).** Same class, pre-existing, not blocking. The L1 ACCEPT routes it to a family card under #34030 that ux-3 files. That carrier is not among the inputs read here. The seat should confirm it exists.
- **Out of scope (b): `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:50-53` and eval case 11.** These go false when this PR lands. The skill says "Validation and refusal messages still read labels through `t()` … without `fallbackLocale: 'en'` an `en` refusal names a field by its zh-CN row". It is a governed path, outside this diff and outside the claim, and is routed to seat 5 (carrier 6999412689). **Should-fix S3:** land it together with this PR or right after.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):** no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation, no in-app join and no query. Label resolution runs in memory over metadata and the i18n bundle only.
- **Gate verdicts at this head.** 57 check-runs: 38 success, 18 skipped, 1 cancelled, 0 failure. The cancelled run is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)` (id 135413455965). A later run of the same check on the same head, id 135413699032, concluded `success`.
- **Tier consequence of M1.** Once the narrowing arm is declared, this PR sits on the narrowing face. A `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record, with ④, is owed on the re-declared head. This `TIER_DEFAULT` declaration-face record does not stand in for it.

Graded findings:
- **M1, must-fix.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` must become `yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset. The changeset gains the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO migration and exactly one ADR-0087 marker. A full dogfood battery is then owed on the new head, and so is a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` narrowing-face record.
- **S1, should-fix.** The migration's TO side has no named type to write against: `ValidationLabelTranslation` is not re-exported from `.` or `./core`. Export it as a type, or spell `TranslationBundle` and `ResolveOptions` in the migration line.
- **S2, should-fix as a follow-up, not blocking.** The `ResolveOptions` build now exists in four copies: `metaTranslateOptions`, `readerOptionLabels`, `labelTranslationOf` and `denialLabels`. The card picked route (A) to keep one rule in one place. The language rule does live in one place, `translateObject`, but how its options are assembled can drift between the copies. The claim allowed no new helper, so this goes to a follow-up card.
- **S3, should-fix, routed.** The skills sentence and eval case 11 go stale on landing. Carrier 6999412689 already exists.

Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35351`
